# tools: replace Arc with Dia before the Arc cask is disabled

Move the hosts from Arc ([[DOT-471]]) to [Dia](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/thebrowsercompany-dia), the next browser of the same company. **Motivation:** Homebrew deprecated the cask, and every `self-update brew` now ends with the reminder:

```
Warning: arc has been deprecated because it is discontinued upstream! It will be disabled on 2026-12-22.
```

After that date the cask can no longer be installed or upgraded, and Arc itself is reported to shut down the same day, so a host that still lists `cask "arc"` keeps a dead browser and a Brewfile that points at nothing. Dia ships an importer for Arc, which makes it the shortest way out.

Expected: the Brewfiles of OctoMac-Pro, OctoMac-Air and OctoMac-mini install Dia instead of Arc, and the switch loses nothing that lived in Arc on any of them: profiles and spaces, pinned tabs and folders, bookmarks, passwords, history, extensions, and the Arc-only content (Boosts, Easels, Notes) that no importer carries, which ends up saved somewhere it can be found. Arc stays usable on a host until that host has been checked.

Out of scope: choosing a browser other than Dia; changing the browser integrations of other tools beyond pointing them at the new default browser.

<!-- 2026-10-31T00:53Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/904#issuecomment-6566279724
Migration plan. The patch removes `cask "arc"` and adds `cask "thebrowsercompany-dia"`, and `self-update` runs `brew bundle --force-cleanup`, so **the first `self-update` on a host after the merge uninstalls `/Applications/Arc.app`**. That is the point of no return for the app, so everything below happens per host before it, and the order is: back up, take inventory, import, verify, only then let the cleanup run. `brew uninstall` without `--zap` leaves `~/Library/Application Support/Arc` in place, and the backup covers even a zap.

What the importer brings is not settled: third-party write-ups disagree about pinned tabs and extensions, and Dia's own help was not checked. The plan therefore does not trust the importer and compares the result against an inventory made beforehand.

Order of hosts: OctoMac-Pro first (it carries most of the data, 1.0 GB of Arc profile on 2026-10-31), then OctoMac-Air, then OctoMac-mini. Each host is done on its own: Arc Sync carries the sidebar between Macs, but passwords, history, extensions and local data are per host.

1. **Back up.** Quit Arc (`osascript -e 'quit app "Arc"'`), then archive the profile and the settings:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p ~/Backups
   ditto -c -k --keepParent ~/Library/Application\ Support/Arc ~/Backups/arc-"$(uname -n | sed 's/\.local$//')"-"$(date +%F)".zip
   cp ~/Library/Preferences/company.thebrowser.Browser.plist ~/Backups/
   ```
   Check that the archive opens (`unzip -tq <archive>`). Keep it at least until spring 2027, outside anything that self-update or CleanMyMac cleans.
2. **Inventory**, written down so it can be compared afterwards: the profiles (`User Data/Default`, `User Data/Profile *`), the spaces and the pinned tabs and folders of each, the extensions (`arc://extensions`), the number of saved passwords (`arc://settings/passwords`), payment methods and addresses, Boosts, Easels, Notes, Little Arc and Air Traffic Control rules, and any tab still open that is not pinned (Arc archives it, and the archive is not imported).
3. **Save what no importer carries.** Copy the code of each Boost, export or copy Easels and Notes, write down the Air Traffic Control rules. Passwords that live only in Arc go to 1Password first; if that needs Arc's CSV export, the CSV is deleted right after the import into 1Password.
4. **Install Dia next to Arc**: `brew install --cask thebrowsercompany-dia` — the same name as in the patch, so `brew bundle` later sees it as installed.
5. **Import**: in Dia's onboarding, or Settings → Import → Arc, with Arc closed and its data in place.
6. **Verify against the inventory**: profiles and spaces, pinned tabs and folders, bookmarks, the number of passwords, history, extensions (whatever did not come is installed again from the Chrome Web Store, including the 1Password extension), and the logins of the services used daily (cookies may not transfer; make sure two-factor is at hand before logging out anywhere).
7. **Switch the defaults**: System Settings → Desktop & Dock → Default web browser → Dia, then whatever opens Arc by name (Raycast and similar).
8. **Live in Dia for a while with Arc still installed** as the fallback.
9. **Let the cleanup run**: merge the patch once every host has passed steps 1–8, or run each remaining host through them before its first `self-update` after the merge. Do not `brew uninstall --zap arc`; the Arc data directory is removed by hand later, if at all, and the archive from step 1 stays.

Deadline: all hosts through step 9 before 2026-12-22.

Rollback: up to step 9 Arc is untouched and simply stays in use. After step 9 and before 2026-12-22, `brew install --cask arc` brings the app back onto its data in place; after that date the cask is disabled and Arc is gone anyway, and what remains is the data in the archive of step 1.
-->
